classification: community-measured; cross-check against the shipped client/decompile before any retail-fidelity claim
immutabilityNote: Named -20b because wa-community-2026-08-20 was taken earlier the SAME DAY and is immutable and checksum-verified. NEITHER of the earlier snapshots was read-modified or written to by this session.
whyThisSnapshotExists: findings-material-mass.md section 1.2 records that one sheet in this lineage is already HTTP 410 and permanently lost, with three of its four tabs unrecoverable. Every source here is one owner-deletion from the same fate, so they are copied rather than linked. The sciencesheet.xls was fetched FIRST because it is the source of the mass table the server ships.
epochWarning: Two DIFFERENT PATCH EPOCHS are represented in this directory and they must never be mixed. FINAL ERA (what WAReborn ships): sciencesheet.xls - aluminium 0.33, iron 0.39, tungsten 0.70, gold 0.73. CALCULATOR ERA: Metal Chart and Fureniku - aluminium 0.26, iron 0.38, tungsten 0.80, gold 0.69. The orderings differ: the final era puts gold above tungsten, the calculator era the reverse. See docs/research/findings-material-mass.md and Multiplayer/Materials/MaterialMassEpoch.cs.
retrievalNotes: worldsadrift.fandom.com HTML returns 403 to curl; .../api.php?action=parse&page=X&format=json&prop=wikitext returns 200 and is the way in.
All ten fetches returned HTTP 200. No source in this snapshot was walled, rate-limited or partially recovered.
Google Sheets /export?format=csv returns only the DEFAULT tab unless a gid is given. Where only one tab was fetched, that is what is held - other tabs of those workbooks are NOT archived.

workbooks.significance: THE EPOCH TRAP CAUGHT IN THE WILD, and the provenance of our own lift column. One table carries calculator-era weights (titanium 0.30, iron 0.38, tungsten 0.80, aluminium 0.26) beside the atlas lift rates we actually ship (titanium 1, steel 1.5, lead 2, bronze 2.5, iron 3, tungsten 3.5, nickel 4, tin 4.5, aluminium 6, copper 7.5). It also reproduces iron's anomalous +1 max lift (61, not 60), confirming that as a source quirk rather than our transcription error.
